query: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs phase stability and why, with relevance to retaining desirable combinations of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries of the hypothesis, supporting prior evidence, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, phase stability is governed by the percolation of Ni–Al B2-like chemical short-range order (CSRO). When Ni–Al CSRO clusters remain sub-percolating, the alloy is stabilized as a single-phase FCC solid solution that retains a favorable combination of cryogenic toughness, radiation tolerance, and acceptable oxidation resistance. When CSRO clusters percolate (via increased Al activity or thermal exposure), the free-energy minimum shifts to long-range B2 ordering and/or FCC+B2 two-phase states, increasing high-temperature strength and alumina-scale formation but degrading cryogenic toughness and radiation tolerance.
generation.material_initial_state: AlxCoCrFeNi with x ≈ 0.10 (at. fraction of Al), Co/Cr/Fe/Ni near-equiatomic, vacuum-melted, homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h in Ar, water-quenched to minimize ordering; single-phase FCC confirmed by XRD and no superlattice reflections.
generation.intervention: Induce controlled changes in Ni–Al CSRO at fixed composition by isothermal aging at 600–700 °C (24–72 h) versus water quench, and, in a parallel arm, increase Al from x=0.10 to x=0.15 under identical thermal histories to push CSRO toward/over a percolation threshold.
generation.conditions: Processing: 1200 °C homogenization, water quench; aging at 600–700 °C in Ar. Characterization and tests: room-temperature and 77 K tensile tests; in-situ TEM to estimate SFE via partial dislocation separations; 700–900 °C microhardness/creep surrogates; 1000 °C dry-air isothermal oxidation (24–100 h); 3 MeV Ni ion irradiation at RT to ~10 dpa; synchrotron diffuse scattering and HAADF-STEM to quantify CSRO.
generation.structural_mediator: Extent and connectivity (correlation length and volume fraction) of Ni–Al B2-like CSRO, quantified by intensity and spatial distribution of B2 superlattice diffuse scattering, pair-correlation functions from atom probe for Ni–Al pairs, and the emergence of discrete B2 superlattice reflections (onset of long-range order).
generation.mechanism: Ni–Al B2-like CSRO locally lowers the enthalpy for B2 bonding. Below a connectivity threshold, these clusters remain isolated, preserving a high-entropy FCC matrix while modestly reducing stacking-fault energy and providing chemical traps that aid defect recombination. Once CSRO clusters percolate (via higher Al activity or sufficient thermal exposure), the configurational-entropy advantage is overcome, promoting long-range B2 ordering/precipitation and a FCC+B2 microstructure. Sub-percolation CSRO supports twinning-mediated plasticity and defect sink behavior; supra-percolation ordering raises ordering (APB) energies and impedes partials, trading cryogenic toughness and radiation tolerance for higher high-temperature strength and improved external Al2O3 scale formation.
generation.predicted_outcome:
- Relative to a quenched x=0.10 baseline (low CSRO, single-phase FCC):
  • Aging at 600–700 °C increases Ni–Al CSRO signals without distinct B2 reflections; SFE decreases modestly; more deformation twinning at 77 K; similar or slightly higher yield strength with retained high elongation; reduced post-irradiation loop density/hardening compared to baseline; oxidation shows a shift toward Al-enriched mixed oxides but not a fully continuous alumina scale.
  • Increasing Al to x=0.15 and aging promotes percolation: discrete B2 superlattice reflections and/or nanoscale B2 precipitates appear; high-temperature hardness/creep resistance increases; 77 K ductility and toughness decrease (less twinning/more planar slip or early localization); irradiation defect persistence and hardening increase; oxidation transitions toward a more continuous Al2O3-rich scale with lower mass gain than baseline.
  • At identical composition, samples with higher quantified CSRO connectivity trend toward the two-phase/B2 state and property trade-offs; those with lower connectivity remain single-phase FCC with balanced properties.
generation.baseline: Al0.10CoCrFeNi, homogenized at 1200 °C and water-quenched, single-phase FCC with minimal Ni–Al CSRO (no B2 superlattice reflections; weak diffuse B2 scattering).
generation.boundary: Expected to hold for Al contents ~5–15 at% and thermal exposures that do not form TCP phases; outside this window: (i) at Al < ~5 at%, CSRO is too sparse to influence phase stability measurably; (ii) at Al > ~20 at% or with prolonged high-temperature exposure, long-range B2 ordering dominates regardless of initial CSRO; (iii) concurrent formation of sigma/TCP phases or severe segregation invalidates the CSRO-percolation control.
generation.uncertainty: The exact CSRO percolation threshold (in terms of correlation length/volume fraction) and its quantitative effect on SFE and defect kinetics are uncertain and may depend on Co/Cr/Fe partitioning and anti-site disorder. Competing transformations (e.g., sigma) could mask or override CSRO-driven behavior under some conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare four conditions: (A) x=0.10 quenched; (B) x=0.10 aged 600–700 °C to raise CSRO without precipitates; (C) x=0.15 quenched; (D) x=0.15 aged to promote CSRO percolation. Quantify Ni–Al CSRO (diffuse scattering, APT pair correlations), check for B2 reflections/precipitates (synchrotron XRD, TEM), and measure SFE (in-situ TEM), 77 K tensile response, high-T microhardness, 3 MeV Ni-ion irradiation defect density/hardening, and 1000 °C oxidation mass gain/scale chemistry.
measurements: Synchrotron diffuse scattering intensity around B2 superlattice positions and emergence of superlattice peaks
Atom-probe Ni–Al pair-correlation functions and CSRO parameters
HAADF-STEM FFTs and real-space mapping of ordered domains; precipitate size/volume fraction if present
SFE from partial dislocation separations in TEM
77 K tensile yield strength and uniform elongation; evidence of twinning
Ion-irradiation defect loop density and irradiation-induced hardening
1000 °C oxidation mass gain and scale phase identification (Raman/XRD/XPS cross-sections)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Falsify if either: (i) at fixed composition, large changes in quantified Ni–Al CSRO connectivity do not correlate with the predicted shifts in phase state (single-phase FCC versus FCC+B2) and property trends (SFE/twinning, irradiation defect retention, oxidation behavior); or (ii) B2 long-range order/precipitation appears without prior increase in Ni–Al CSRO connectivity toward a percolation-like state.
